name: FORALL Parallel Assignment (F95)
description: Multi-index parallel assignment with RHS-before-LHS semantics — nested fir.do_loop structure vs DO CONCURRENT
source:
subroutine forall_identity(a, n)
  implicit none
  integer, intent(in)  :: n
  real,    intent(out) :: a(n,n)
  integer :: i, j

  FORALL (i = 1:n, j = 1:n)
    a(i,j) = MERGE(1.0, 0.0, i == j)
  END FORALL

end subroutine forall_identity

Symbol table: forall_identity
  a: rank=2 REAL(4)    intent=IntentOut  shape=(1:n,1:n)
  n: rank=0 INTEGER(4) intent=IntentIn
  i: rank=0 INTEGER(4) FORALL index (local scope)
  j: rank=0 INTEGER(4) FORALL index (local scope)

FORALL analysis:
  Indices: i ∈ [1,n], j ∈ [1,n]  (total n² iterations)
  Body LHS: a(i,j) — subscripts are affine functions of FORALL indices
  Body RHS: MERGE(1.0, 0.0, i==j)
    MERGE: elemental intrinsic, non-recursive, no side effects
    i==j: logical scalar in FORALL body → evaluated per iteration
  Two-phase semantics: ALL RHS expressions evaluated BEFORE any LHS assignment
    Flang implements this via temporary array allocation when needed
    Here: MERGE is pure → no temporary needed; emitted as nested loop
  FORALL vs DO CONCURRENT:
    DO CONCURRENT: independence is user-declared
    FORALL: independence is compiler-verified from subscript analysis

llvm_ir.content:
; ModuleID = '04_forall.f90'
source_filename = "04_forall.f90"
target triple = "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"

define void @_QPforall_identity(
    ptr nocapture %0,           ; a(n,n)
    ptr nocapture readonly %1   ; n
) #0 !dbg !5 {
entry:
  %n_val = load i32, ptr %1, align 4, !dbg !10
  %n_ext = sext i32 %n_val to i64
  %guard = icmp sgt i64 %n_ext, 0
  br i1 %guard, label %outer.ph, label %exit

outer.ph:
  br label %outer

outer:                          ; i loop
  %i = phi i64 [ 1, %outer.ph ], [ %i.next, %inner.latch ], !dbg !11
  br label %inner

inner:                          ; j loop
  %j = phi i64 [ 1, %outer ], [ %j.next, %inner ], !dbg !11

  ; MERGE(1.0, 0.0, i==j) → icmp + select (no branch)
  %ieqj   = icmp eq i64 %i, %j, !dbg !12
  %result = select i1 %ieqj, float 1.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, !dbg !12

  ; Fortran column-major: a(i,j) → base + (j-1)*n + (i-1)
  %j_1    = sub nsw i64 %j, 1
  %i_1    = sub nsw i64 %i, 1
  %col_off= mul nsw i64 %j_1, %n_ext
  %offset = add nsw i64 %col_off, %i_1
  %a_ptr  = getelementptr inbounds float, ptr %0, i64 %offset, !dbg !12
  store float %result, ptr %a_ptr, align 4, !dbg !12

  %j.next = add nuw nsw i64 %j, 1
  %j_done = icmp eq i64 %j.next, %n_ext
  br i1 %j_done, label %inner.latch, label %inner

inner.latch:
  %i.next = add nuw nsw i64 %i, 1
  %i_done = icmp eq i64 %i.next, %n_ext
  br i1 %i_done, label %exit, label %outer

exit:
  ret void, !dbg !13
}

; Note: column-major GEP = base + (j-1)*n + (i-1)
; This is the critical difference from C row-major: j is the outer stride.

correlations.lowering_notes: FORALL with two indices becomes a 2-D hlfir.elemental in HLFIR — the block argument carries both loop variables. Unlike DO CONCURRENT, FORALL does not carry the 'unordered' attribute because the Fortran standard's two-phase semantics (all RHS before LHS) requires a sequential view. However Flang proves independence here via subscript analysis and omits the temporary. The LLVM GEP uses column-major addressing: offset = (j-1)*n + (i-1).

MERGE is an elemental intrinsic that maps directly to arith.select — no function call generated. The i==j comparison on FORALL indices uses arith.cmpi (integer compare) since loop indices are of type 'index' in MLIR. This produces a branchless select in LLVM IR, ideal for vectorization.

lowering_patterns.name: FORALL → 2-D hlfir.elemental
lowering_patterns.description: Multi-index FORALL constructs map to a single hlfir.elemental with a multi-dimensional shape; the block arguments carry all index variables simultaneously, matching the construct's parallel semantics

lowering_patterns.name: Fortran Column-Major GEP
lowering_patterns.description: 2-D array element a(i,j) generates GEP offset = (j-1)*n + (i-1) — the opposite of C's row-major. The compiler adjusts the base pointer for 1-based Fortran indexing by subtracting n+1 from the base

lowering_patterns.name: MERGE Intrinsic → arith.select
lowering_patterns.description: Fortran's MERGE elemental intrinsic compiles to a single MLIR arith.select operation — no conditional branch, enabling SIMD vectorization with blend instructions
